full_judgment:
2. The appellant-petitioner has been convicted under section 25B of the Special Powers Act and sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 1 (one) year and 6 months and to pay a fine of Tk. 3,000.00, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for 3 (three) months more by the Assistant Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal No. 2, Thakurgaon, in Special Tribunal Case No. 19 of 1989, by his judgment and order dated 29.11.89. 

 4. Admittedly there is a delay of 38 days in filing the Criminal Appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act. Now question is whether an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the said appeal is maintainable in view of section 29(2) of the Limitation Act. This point has been elaborately discussed and decided by a Division Bench of this Court. In the case of Elahi Bux Vs. The State reported in 39 DLR at page 164, it has been held differing with a Single Bench decision reported in 1985 BO page 335 that section 5 of the Limitation Act has no manner of application for condonation of delay in filing an appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act, 1974, and that being a decision of the Division Bench I am bound by the same. Hence whatever may be the merit of the application I must hold that this application for condonation of delay under section 5 of the Limitation Act filed on behalf of the appellant-petitioner is not at all maintainable. 

 5. Mr. Md. Abdul Majid, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant-petitioner, however, contends that if the Memo of Appeal cannot be entertained, the same being out of time by 38 days, this Court can treat this petition of appeal as a revisional application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in that case it will be within the period of limitation. In support of this contention Mr. Majid has referred to two decisions reported in 9 DLR 424 and 23 DLR (Peshwar) 12. In the case of Rahman Gut Vs. The State reported in 23 DLR (Peshwar) 12. It has been held that : 

 6. In the reported case, the appellant along with his father were tried under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and ultimately the father was acquitted but the son appellant was convicted under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced to transportation for life and a fine of Rs. 1,000.00 or in default to suffer 2 years RI further. The appellant Rahman Gul preferred a jail appeal beyond the statutory period of 60 days of limitation and there was no application even under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of the delay and obviously the appeal was barred by limitation. Their Lordships on perusal of the Judgment of the Trial Court and the record of the case were satisfied that there was serious miscarriage of justice in the trial. 

 7. Hence in exercise of their jurisdiction under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, entertained the petition of appeal as a revisional application. But in the instant case the appellant has been tried under a Special Law, namely, the Special Powers Act, 1974 and convicted and sentenced there under. The Act provides only for appeal against order, Judgment or sentence of the Special Tribunal within 30 days from the date of delivery or passing thereof as amended upto date. Nowhere in this Act there is any provision for revision in the High Court Division against order, judgment or sentence passed by the Special Tribunal. In this view of the matter the decision reported in 23 DLR (Peshwar) 12 has no manner of application in this case. 

 8. Now, let me see how far the decision in the case of Rustom Ali Mia Bhuiyan Vs. The State reported in 9 DLR 424 can be availed of by the learned Advocate for the appellant-petitioner. In this reported case a proceeding under section 514 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was started against the appellant in a case under the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948. The appellant preferred an appeal from an order made under section 514 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but in fact the impugned order was not appealable but revisable. It was contended that sub-section (1) of section 9 of the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948 provides for both appeal and revision in the High Court against the Judgment passed by a Special Judge. Sub-section (1) of section 9 of the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948 reads as follows : 

 And in that view of the matter, the appeal wrongly filed by the appellant was treated as a revisional application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the ends of justice. In the instant case there is no provision of appeal as well as revision, as in sub-section (1) of section 9 of the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948. There is only one provision for appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act against any order, judgment or sentence passed thereunder. So, the above reported case is also distinguishable from the present one. Therefore, this decision of the 9 DLR case has also no application in the present case. 

 9. Lastly Mr. Majid has referred to a decision in the case of Abul Hossain and others Vs. The State reported in 37 DLR 59 which again has relied upon a decision in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Shahjahan Seraj reported in 32 DLR (AD) 1 where it has been held that, 

 "although this Court has no power to revise any order, judgment or sentence passed under the Special Powers Act but this Court has jurisdiction under section 561A CrPC in an appropriate case under the Special Powers Act to prevent the abuse of the process of any Court to secure the ends of justice." 

 10. In the above decision, question was whether an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure against a judgment and order passed by the Appellate Tribunal in a Tribunal Appeal was maintainable or not. But in the instant case the question is different. Here it is an application for condonation of delay under section 5 of the Limitation Act arising out of a Criminal Appeal filed out of time against the judgment and order of a Special Tribunal under the Special Powers Act. So the premises of these two cases are absolutely different and as such this decision reported in 37 DLR has also no manner of application in this case. 

 11. Mr. Md. Sajjad Ali Chowdhury, the learned Assistant Attorney-General being invited by this Court, submits on behalf of the State that the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the Criminal Appeal is not at all maintainable and he further submits that in view of the absence of any specific power of revision to this Court by the Special Powers Act against any order, judgment or sentence passed thereunder, this petition of appeal cannot be treated as a revisional application and the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner are not at all applicable in the present case.
